newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagreb says will resist pressure for Yugo union.
newsitem.headline: Zagreb says will resist pressure for Yugo union.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman on Wednesday welcomed his country's admission to the Council of Europe, but warned of "new tragedies" if the West continues to push for strong ties between former Yugoslav republics.

Addressing the nation in a live television broadcast hours after the Council announced it had accepted Croatia as its 40th member, Tudjman said he hoped his country would also be able to join the European Union soon.
The Council of Europe is considered to be the antechamber to the European Union, an organisation that Tudjman's government has longed to join.

But the Croatian president warned Zagreb would not accept the EU's "regional approach" which he claims is a demand for the former Yugoslav republics to boost economic cooperation, introduce soft borders and establish a kind of common market.
"The enforcement of an untenable regional framework -- not in the distant but in near future -- could cause new tragic events," he said.
Tudjman said Croatia would never be pushed into anything reminiscent of the former Yugoslavia, which violently broke up in 1991, following the secesssion of Croatia and neighbouring Slovenia.
"If there is any insistance on such regional unions then Croatia's place is with central European countries, from the Baltic to the Adriatic sea."
Croatia is the third former Yugoslav republic to join the Council of Europe, which seeks to promote democracy and human rights, after Slovenia and Macedonia.
The Strasbourg-based Council froze Croatia's application last May and set conditions concerning democracy, press freedom, and respect for the Dayton peace agreement which ended the war in Bosnia.
